haiku-low.q1: They do not differ visibly. Both get 401 with "Invalid email or password". A dummy bcrypt hash keeps timing similar for unknown emails.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 on the login page with a too-many-attempts message and Retry-After seconds. No password check runs, and the attempt is not counted or extending the lock.
haiku-low.q3: The existing session named by the cookie is deleted in the same transaction, and a new session is inserted with a new ID. Login always rotates.
haiku-low.q4: Only the opaque random session ID travels in the __Host-sid cookie. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: The 30-minute idle limit restarts on each request, but the 12-hour absolute limit from login is fixed. The session stops working 12 hours after login.
haiku-low.q6: The shared check finds zero rows, so the server redirects with 302 to /login and clears the cookie. The route does not run.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session by the cookie's hash, then replies 302 to /login with the cookie cleared. If the session is already gone, the reply is the same.
haiku-low.q8: Session state is kept in Postgres's sessions table. Any app instance queries the shared database, so both instances see the same sessions.
haiku-low.q9: Each normalized email's failures are in the login_failures table as the last 5 timestamps. A failure within 10 minutes of now locks the email, using Postgres now().
haiku-low.q10: It checks last_seen_at against 30 minutes ago and absolute_expires_at against now(), using Postgres now(). When valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns the user ID.
haiku-low.q11: The browser gets 503 on the login page saying it could not sign in, with no cookie issued. The old session and failure count stay unchanged.
haiku-low.q12: A cleanup timer on each app instance runs every 10 minutes and deletes sessions past the idle or absolute limit, plus stale failure rows.

sonnet.q1: It does not differ. Both get 401 login page with "Invalid email or password", and the dummy bcrypt hash keeps timing the same.
sonnet.q2: It is locked: the server returns 429 login page (too many attempts) with Retry-After set to seconds left, before any password check. The attempt is not counted and does not extend the lock.
sonnet.q3: On successful login, the old session named by the cookie is deleted in the same transaction that inserts the new session, even if the cookie was valid. A new session ID is set in the cookie.
sonnet.q4: Only an opaque random session ID (32 random bytes, base64url). Page scripts cannot read it because it is HttpOnly.
sonnet.q5: At the 12-hour absolute limit after login, regardless of activity. Idle renewal does not extend it.
sonnet.q6: The update returns zero rows, so the server responds 302 to /login with the cookie cleared.
sonnet.q7: If a cookie is present, it deletes the session row by hash of the cookie. Then it replies 302 to /login with the cookie cleared. If the session is already gone, the delete affects zero rows and the reply is the same.
sonnet.q8: In Postgres, in the sessions table, which both app instances share. The instance hashes the cookie value (SHA-256) and looks up the row by id_hash.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, one row per normalized email, holding the last 5 failure times and an optional locked_until. On a failure, if there are 5 entries and the oldest is within 10 minutes (using Postgres now()), it sets a 15-minute lock.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at to now() minus 30 minutes (idle limit) and absolute_expires_at to now(), using Postgres now(). If both hold, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns the user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 login page: "We could not sign you in right now. Try again in a moment." No cookie is issued.
sonnet.q12: The cleanup timer on each app instance, every 10 minutes, deletes sessions where last_seen_at is at least 30 minutes old or absolute_expires_at has passed.
